text.p: Bonds closed below their highs and the longer end was likely to follow the Spanish trend on Tuesday with the spread remaining between five and 10 basis points.

Traders said the futures saw some rollovers from December into March but the market ended up relatively cheap compared to the cash. They saw the cash market at the long end holding to a spread of five to 10 basis points below the Spanish equivalent.
"If Spain widens the differential with Germany, we will follow but the spread (with Spain) will widen to a negative 10 basis points," said one trader.
The 10-year spread with Germany was not seen widening beyond 110 basis points.
Traders said that the market would be likely to remain cautious on Tuesday head of the Federal Open Market Committee even if no change in U.S. rates was expected.
The 0.9 percent rise in U.S. industrial output in November was higher than expected but "a U.S. rate rise is only likely in 1997," said one trader.
